rem:u-spin-coleman-glashow:
Remark U-spin and the Coleman–Glashow relation: a third null result. Beyond isospin, the flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} contains two further \mathrm{SU}(2) subgroups: U-spin, exchanging d \leftrightarrow s, and V-spin, exchanging u \leftrightarrow s. U-spin is the useful one, because the electric charge is invariant under it --- d and s both carry Q = -\tfrac{1}{3} --- which makes the electromagnetic interaction a U-spin scalar.

The classical consequence is the Coleman--Glashow relation among the baryon octet's electromagnetic splittings,

  \bigl(\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}}\bigr)
  - \bigl(\mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^+} - \mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^-}\bigr)
  + \bigl(\mathfrak{m}_{\Xi^0} - \mathfrak{m}_{\Xi^-}\bigr)
  = 0,

which experiment satisfies to -0.064 MeV against splittings of 1.3 to 8.1 MeV --- about 0.8\% of the largest.

The relation carries no information about the breaking mechanism. This is a theorem: the combination vanishes for every choice of the six first-order parameters, over any commutative ring , so two arbitrarily different breaking patterns give the same answer.

Why it vanishes

Two standard premises, and both are needed. First, isospin is exact in the strong sector, so the strong mass depends only on the isospin multiplet --- one parameter each for (\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n}), (\Sigma^+, \Sigma^-) and (\Xi^0, \Xi^-). Second, the electromagnetic self-energy is a U-spin scalar, hence constant on a U-spin multiplet.

The octet's U-spin multiplets are exactly the pairs the relation uses, each at fixed charge, which is why the relation pairs the states it does:

U-spin multiplet Quark content Q EM shift
\mathfrak{p} \leftrightarrow \Sigma^+ uud \leftrightarrow uus +1 a
\mathfrak{n} \leftrightarrow \Xi^0 udd \leftrightarrow uss 0 b
\Sigma^- \leftrightarrow \Xi^- dds \leftrightarrow dss -1 c

Six parameters --- three strong, three electromagnetic --- and the alternating combination cancels every one: a appears in \mathfrak{p} and \Sigma^+ with opposite sign, b in \mathfrak{n} and \Xi^0, c in \Sigma^- and \Xi^-. Switching the electromagnetic shifts off makes each splitting vanish separately, so the relation is empty without electromagnetism rather than being a statement about the strong sector.

One difference from the other two null results

Gell-Mann--Okubo and the decuplet equal-spacing rule each follow from a single premise. Coleman--Glashow rests on a conjunction. Dropping the U-spin premise --- letting the electromagnetic shift differ between the two members of a multiplet --- makes the combination equal the difference of those two shifts rather than zero , which is detectable.

The relation therefore does test that the electromagnetic self-energy is U-spin invariant and that isospin is exact in the strong sector. What it cannot do is distinguish among the mechanisms satisfying both, and the framework has offered no reason to doubt either premise. Reproducing Coleman--Glashow would therefore be no evidence for this framework, or for any other.

What remains testable

On the microscopic connected Borromean V^3 pairwise charge trace at strand charges u = +\tfrac{2}{3} and d = s = -\tfrac{1}{3}, all three doublet splittings \mathfrak{p} - \mathfrak{n}, \Sigma^+ - \Sigma^-, and \Xi^0 - \Xi^- evaluate to distinct non-zero rational functions of q while their alternating Coleman--Glashow sum vanishes identically, illustrating the identity directly on the baryon braid word without free parameters.

What remains testable is the residual, as with the other two. At \approx 0.8\% it is the tightest of the three --- against \approx 6.4\% for Gell-Mann--Okubo on the pseudoscalar octet and \approx 9.2\% for the decuplet spacings --- which makes it the most demanding second-order target and the least likely to be reached first. V-spin (u \leftrightarrow s) yields no independent relation for the octet and is not treated separately.
prop:baryon-octet-decomposition:
Proposition The baryon octet and the degeneracy of its weight diagram. The mixed channel \lambda = (2,1) of V^{\otimes 3} carries the baryon octet. Unlike the decuplet, its weight diagram is degenerate --- and that degeneracy is the one piece of eightfold-way structure in this chapter which constrains rather than describes.

Conditional on N = 3 (Proposition), the three-fold product decomposes as

  \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3}
  \;=\;
  \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1},
  \qquad
  27 = 10 \cdot 1 + 8 \cdot 2 + 1 \cdot 1 .

The two octets are one flavour irrep counted with the multiplicity \dim S^{(2,1)} = 2 of its Hecke partner, not two different multiplets. The decuplet is treated in the preceding proposition; the octet is the subject here.

The eight states

Writing the weight as (2I_3, Y) keeps every entry an integer.

State Content 2I_3 Y I
\mathfrak{p} uud +1 +1 1/2
\mathfrak{n} udd -1 +1 1/2
\Sigma^{+} uus +2 0 1
\Sigma^{0} uds 0 0 1
\Lambda uds 0 0 0
\Sigma^{-} dds -2 0 1
\Xi^{0} uss +1 -1 1/2
\Xi^{-} dss -1 -1 1/2

\Sigma^0 and \Lambda share both the quark content uds and the weight (0,0). They are separated only by isospin, I = 1 against I = 0. The octet's eight states therefore occupy seven lattice points: six on the hexagon and two stacked at the centre.

The degeneracy is a constraint

Every other eightfold relation this chapter examines --- Gell-Mann--Okubo, the decuplet equal-spacing rule and Coleman--Glashow --- turns out to be an identity of its first-order ansatz, true for all parameter values and therefore evidence for no mechanism. This one is different, and the difference is proved:

  • The decuplet's ten weights are pairwise distinct ; the octet's eight are not , with exactly one collision, at the origin .
  • Hence no function of the weight alone can separate \Lambda from \Sigma^0. The statement holds for an arbitrary target, not for real-valued masses alone . Any mass formula built from (2I_3, Y) predicts \mathfrak{m}_\Lambda = \mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^0}.

Experiment gives \mathfrak{m}_\Lambda \approx 1115.7 MeV against \mathfrak{m}_{\Sigma^0} \approx 1192.6 MeV --- a 77 MeV gap, about 7\%, two orders of magnitude larger than the 0.8\% Coleman--Glashow residual. The class is excluded outright.

This is a scope-(b) structural exclusion, and the invariant justifying it is proved rather than asserted: non-injectivity of the weight map on the octet. The obligation it creates falls on every framework, this one included --- a label beyond (2I_3, Y) must be supplied. Physically that label is isospin, which is demonstrably not a function of the weight . The decuplet incurs no such obligation , which is precisely why its equal-spacing rule runs on Y alone while Gell-Mann--Okubo needs the isospin Casimir as well.

Two twos, kept apart, and the diquark projector split

The multiplicity \dim S^{(2,1)} = 2 and the \Lambda/\Sigma^0 degeneracy are distinct phenomena: the first counts copies of the eight-dimensional flavour irrep inside V^{\otimes 3}, whereas the second counts two states over the (0,0) weight inside one copy. Within the two-dimensional mixed-symmetry Hecke module S^{(2,1)} itself, however, the (1,2) diquark exchange \sigma_1 has distinct eigenvalues -q^{-1} (I = 0, antisymmetric ud diquark for \Lambda) and +q (I = 1, symmetric ud diquark for \Sigma^0), supplying two mutually orthogonal rank-1 idempotents

  P_\Lambda = [2]_q^{-1}(q - \sigma_1),
  \qquad
  P_{\Sigma^0} = [2]_q^{-1}(\sigma_1 + q^{-1}),
  \qquad
  P_\Lambda + P_{\Sigma^0} = 1_{S^{(2,1)}},

whose traces match the 3 \times 3 baryon weight-space sub-projectors across \sigma_1, \sigma_2, V = \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}, and V^3. On the commuting Jucys--Murphy twists J_2 = \sigma_1^2 and J_3 = \sigma_2\sigma_1^2 \sigma_2 ([J_2, J_3] = 0), \mathrm{tr}(P_{\Sigma^0} J_2) = q^2 and \mathrm{tr}(P_\Lambda J_2) = q^{-2}; on a single Borromean step, \mathrm{tr}(P_{\Sigma^0} V) = q^6\,\mathrm{tr}(P_\Lambda V); and on the full Borromean baryon braid V^3 = (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^3, the zero-parameter diquark splitting is

  \mathrm{tr}(P_\Lambda V^3) - \mathrm{tr}(P_{\Sigma^0} V^3)
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q - q^{-1})^3 (q^2 + q^{-2}) [3]_q}{[2]_q}.

At q_0, this cubic-in-h_0 Borromean trace difference equals +0.028265 (|\mathrm{tr}(P_\Lambda V^3)| / |\mathrm{tr}(P_{\Sigma^0} V^3)| = 1.02875), lifting the weight-only degeneracy without fitted parameters while under-predicting the observed 76.959\;\mathrm{MeV} (6.90\%) gap at 31.53\;\mathrm{MeV} (-59.0\%), whereas the single-crossing ratio q_0 = 1.10998 over-predicts at 122.70\;\mathrm{MeV} (+59.4\%).

What the framework supplies

The decomposition above, and everything drawn from it, is conditional on N = 3. The framework's single-fibre construction gives \dim V = 2, at which the Schur--Weyl row cap removes the singlet entirely and there is no octet to carry a weight diagram --- a proved obstruction, not an approximation (Proposition). No construction here supplies N = 3, and no parameter is fitted to the empirical hadron masses: what is established is that weight-only formulas are excluded structurally, while the internal H_3(q_0) diquark sub-projectors split \Lambda from \Sigma^0 at order (q_0 - q_0^{-1})^3 without closing the quantitative 77\;\mathrm{MeV} scale.
def:octonion-algebra:
Definition The octonion algebra \mathbb{O}. The octonion algebra \mathbb{O} is the 8-dimensional unital algebra with basis e_0, e_1, \dots, e_7, in which e_0 is the unit, each imaginary basis element squares to -1,

  e_i^2 = -1 \qquad (1 \le i \le 7),

and the imaginary units multiply by the cyclic rule

  e_i \, e_{i+1} = e_{i+3},
  \qquad
  e_{i+1} \, e_i = -e_{i+3},

with indices read modulo 7 on \{1, \dots, 7\}, extended to all of \mathbb{O} by bilinearity.

The algebra is alternative — every subalgebra generated by two elements is associative — but not associative: (e_1 e_2) e_4 = -e_1 (e_2 e_4). It carries the norm N(x) = \sum_i x_i^2, which is multiplicative, making \mathbb{O} a normed division algebra. Its automorphism group is the compact 14-dimensional exceptional Lie group G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}), equivalently \mathrm{Der}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathfrak{g}_2 [baez2002].

Convention. The sign rule above is the Baez convention [baez2002], matching the multiplication fixed throughout this work. The choice is not canonical: 480 distinct multiplication tables are compatible with e_0 = 1 and e_i^2 = -1, all isomorphic as algebras but differing in which triples are quaternionic. Any statement that names a specific e_i e_j = \pm e_k is convention-dependent and must carry this qualification; statements about \mathbb{O} up to isomorphism, including \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) = G_2, are not [albuquerque-majid1999].

Base ring. The product is realised over \mathbb{Q} in exact rational arithmetic. Nothing archimedean is required: the structure constants are integers, and the derivation count needs only \mathrm{char} \ne 2, 3.
prop:color-su3-from-g2:
Proposition Color \mathrm{SU}(3) from octonionic stabilization. The discrete color symmetry \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) arises from the octonionic automorphism group G_2 via the Fano plane, whose incidence structure encodes the octonion multiplication table. The octonion algebra is taken as an external input: it is not constructed from the categorical aether, and the attempt to connect the two --- the bridge group S_4 \subset S_5 \cap \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) carrying local Fano data from the Bring surface to the Klein quartic --- is refuted below.

The S_4 bridge mechanism. The Bring surface \Sigma_4 (genus 4) has automorphism group S_5. The Klein quartic \Sigma_3 (genus 3) has automorphism group \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) of order 168 = 84(3-1), the Hurwitz bound. The group S_4 is the maximal common subgroup:

  1. S_4 \subset S_5 as the stabilizer of one letter (index 5).
  2. S_4 \cong \mathrm{Stab}(\mathrm{pt}) in \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) acting on the 7 Fano points (index 7).

The point stabilizer S_4 preserves the local Fano structure at the fixed point: the 3 lines through that point, encoding the 3 octonion multiplication triples involving the corresponding imaginary unit. Computationally verified :

  • S_4 acts transitively on the 3 lines through the fixed point,
  • S_4 acts transitively on the 4 lines not through the fixed point,
  • S_4 acts transitively on the 6 remaining Fano points,
  • the 3 local lines partition the 6 remaining points into 3 pairs.

Conjectured genus degeneration. The derivation chain from Bring to Fano is:

  \underbrace{\Sigma_4}_{g=4,\; S_5}
  \;\xrightarrow{\text{pinch}}\;
  \underbrace{\Sigma_3^{\mathrm{nod}}}_{g_{\mathrm{arith}}=4,\; S_4}
  \;\xrightarrow{\text{normalize}}\;
  \underbrace{\Sigma_3}_{g=3,\; \mathrm{PSL}(2,7)}

Pinching an S_4-invariant 1-cycle on \Sigma_4 produces a nodal curve of arithmetic genus 4 but geometric genus 3. The S_4 symmetry survives the pinch (it fixes the vanishing cycle). On the normalization \Sigma_3 of genus 3, the Hurwitz bound gives |\mathrm{Aut}| \leq 84(3-1) = 168, which \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) attains.

The gap in this argument. The Hurwitz bound is an upper bound; it does not force the automorphism group to be \mathrm{PSL}(2,7), and the generic genus-3 curve has small or trivial automorphism group. That S_4 embeds in \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) as a point stabilizer shows the enhancement is available, not that it occurs: nothing here rules out the normalization being a genus-3 curve whose automorphism group is exactly S_4, or any other group containing S_4. Maximality of the enhancement does not select it.

The S_4 bridge cannot select the Klein quartic. A stronger negative than the Hurwitz error: the S_4 datum has no separating power at all. The Fermat quartic x^4 + y^4 + z^4 = 0 is a genus-3 curve whose automorphism group (\mathbb{Z}/4)^2 \rtimes S_3 of order 96 also contains S_4 --- exhibited as V_4 \rtimes S_3 and verified by exact computation in \mathbb{Z}[i] arithmetic (element-order profile \{1{:}1,\, 2{:}9,\, 3{:}8,\, 4{:}6\}, V_4 normal, S_3 inducing the full symmetric action on V_4 \setminus \{1\}). So even a fully correct argument that the normalization has genus 3 and inherits S_4 stops short of the Klein quartic, because at least one other genus-3 curve satisfies both conditions.

The competitor set is in fact infinite. Fermat is not an isolated coincidence. The S_4-invariant ternary quartics form a two-dimensional space, so the genus-3 curves admitting S_4 contain an entire pencil

C_t : x^4 + y^4 + z^4 + t\,(x^2 y^2 + y^2 z^2 + z^2 x^2) = 0 ,

with parameter t (not \lambda, which throughout this chapter denotes a partition), smooth --- hence of genus 3 --- for every t outside \{2,\, -2,\, -1\}, with Fermat the single member t = 0. The fibres of t \mapsto [C_t] in moduli are finite, so infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic genus-3 curves carry a faithful S_4 action. All of this is machine-verified in exact rational arithmetic, and only finiteness of the automorphism group is used --- the sharp Hurwitz bound is deliberately avoided here, for the reason given above. The S_4 bridge therefore fails not only to choose between two candidates, but to cut a \mathbb{P}^1 down at all.

Identifying the normalization therefore cannot be reduced to telling Klein and Fermat apart. Many invariants do that --- the automorphism-group order alone separates them, 168 against 96 --- while saying nothing about the rest of the family, and nothing whatever about which member the pinch produces. What is required is an invariant that the degeneration itself determines: read off the pinched cycle and the nodal curve, rather than computed from a shortlist of candidate targets. The decisive version is the period matrix. None has been computed. This is a scope-(a) negative: the degeneration itself is not refuted, only the argument offered for it.

The marked points obstruct the degeneration. There is extra data the pinch does supply, and it settles the question --- against the conjecture. Pinching a single non-separating cycle on a genus-4 curve yields a one-node curve of arithmetic genus 4 whose normalization has genus 3 together with two marked points --- the two preimages of the node, consistent with 3 + 1 = 4. Since the pinched cycle is S_4-invariant, S_4 preserves that pair setwise, so the object the degeneration produces is a pair (\Sigma_3, \{p, q\}) with an S_4-stable point pair, not a bare genus-3 curve.

No smooth plane quartic admits such a pair. Let \{p, q\} be S_4-stable; permuting it gives a homomorphism S_4 \to S_2 whose kernel has index 1 or 2, hence is S_4 itself or the unique index-2 subgroup A_4. Either way the line through p is an invariant 1-dimensional subspace of \mathbb{C}^3. But the 3-dimensional representation of S_4 is absolutely irreducible, and so is its restriction to A_4 --- each verified two independent ways, by commutant dimension and by character norm . An absolutely irreducible representation has no invariant line over any extension field, so no such pair exists: S_4 has no orbit of size \le 2 on \mathbb{P}^2 at all.

Consequently, under the three premises this chain itself asserts --- one S_4-invariant non-separating cycle (which is what arithmetic genus 4 and geometric genus 3 mean), S_4 acting faithfully on the normalization (which is what "S_4 survives" means), and a non-hyperelliptic normalization (which the Klein quartic is) --- the required configuration does not exist. This is a scope-(b) structural exclusion, licensed by a proved invariant rather than by a numerical near-miss, and unlike the two earlier failures it bears on the conjecture rather than on an argument for it.

What remains are the escapes, named precisely. A hyperelliptic genus-3 normalization is not excluded: its canonical map is 2-to-1 onto a conic, so its automorphisms do not act through \mathrm{PGL}_3 in the manner above, and such curves admitting S_4 do exist. The Klein quartic is not hyperelliptic, so that escape does not recover it. Nor is a pinch with several nodes or of a separating cycle excluded --- but either is a different claim from the one made here. What the argument does not touch at all is the Bring surface: it constrains the target, not the source.

Status: the S_4 bridge mechanism is computationally verified --- that is, S_4 does act on the local Fano data as claimed. The genus degeneration step is a different matter, and it is no longer unproved but excluded: as shown above, under its own three premises it is excluded. A pinch of the kind described cannot deliver a non-hyperelliptic genus-3 normalization, and the Klein quartic is non-hyperelliptic. Rescuing the colour route therefore requires giving up one of the three premises explicitly --- a hyperelliptic target, a multi-node or separating pinch, or a non-faithful S_4 --- and saying which.

\mathrm{PSL}(2,7) representation theory. Computationally verified: the group \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) \cong \mathrm{GL}(3, \mathbb{F}_2) has 6 conjugacy classes and 6 irreducible representations of dimensions

\begin{equation}\label{eq:psl27-irreps}
  \{1, 3, \bar{3}, 6, 7, 8\},
  \qquad
  \sum d_i^2 = 1 + 9 + 9 + 36 + 49 + 64 = 168 = |\mathrm{PSL}(2,7)|.
\end{equation}

The physical interpretation:

\dim Representation Physical role
1 trivial singlet
3 fundamental color triplet (q)
\bar{3} conjugate color antitriplet (\bar{q})
6 \mathrm{Sym}^2(\mathbf{3}) no singlet \Rightarrow complex type
7 natural on \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) imaginary octonions
8 adjoint of \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} gluon octet

The 3 and \bar{3} are complex conjugate (not self-dual), matching the Günaydin--Gürsey decomposition \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) \cong \mathbb{R} \oplus \mathbb{C}^3 under \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2 [gunaydin-gursey1973]. Non-self-duality is what the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate consumes, so this is a load-bearing citation rather than an attribution: a self-dual 3 would carry a singlet in \mathrm{Sym}^2 and fail the gate.

Prior-art positioning. Deriving three-colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} — introduced to resolve baryon antisymmetry by O. W. Greenberg [greenberg1964] and by M. Y. Han and Y. Nambu [han-nambu1965] — as the subgroup of G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) stabilizing a chosen imaginary octonion unit originates with Murat Günaydin and Feza Gürsey [gunaydin-gursey1973]. Subsequent algebraic Standard Model constructions embed colour alongside electroweak symmetries inside division-algebra tensor products \mathbb{R}\otimes\mathbb{C}\otimes\mathbb{H}\otimes\mathbb{O} (Geoffrey M. Dixon [dixon1994]; Cohl Furey [furey2016, furey2018]) or inside the automorphism and structure groups of the exceptional Jordan algebra J_3(\mathbb{O}) (Ivan Todorov and Michel Dubois-Violette [todorov2018, dubois-violette-todorov2018]; Latham Boyle [boyle2020]). In the present paper, \mathbb{O} is likewise an external algebraic input: the single-fibre \mathrm{SU}_q(2) aether does not construct \mathbb{O}, and the S_4 genus-degeneration route from Bring's curve to the Klein quartic is excluded above.
prop:sl-n-color-framing:
Proposition The \mathrm{SU}(N) framing reproduces the one-gluon color factors. Let V be the vector representation of \mathrm{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_N) and let \sigma_i act on V^{\otimes n} by the Jimbo braiding [jimbo1986], with eigenvalue q on \mathrm{Sym}^2 V and -q^{-1} on \Lambda^2 V. Put \sigma_i^{\mathfrak{sl}} := q^{-1/N}\,\sigma_i. Then:

  1. the eigenvalues of \sigma_i^{\mathfrak{sl}} on \mathrm{Sym}^2 V and \Lambda^2 V are q^{2 c_{\mathrm{S}}} and -q^{2 c_{\mathrm{A}}}, where c_R := \tfrac12\bigl(C_2(R) - 2C_F\bigr) is the one-gluon color factor, c_{\mathrm{S}} = \tfrac{N-1}{2N} and c_{\mathrm{A}} = -\tfrac{N+1}{2N};
  2. the eigenvalues of \sigma_i itself are q^{2c_R + 1/N} up to sign;
  3. the ratio c_{\mathrm{A}}/c_{\mathrm{S}} = -\tfrac{N+1}{N-1} equals -2 if and only if N = 3;
  4. q^{-1/N} is the unique positive scalar c for which the monodromy of V around \Lambda^N V under c\,\sigma_i is the identity.

Proof. Items 1--3 are identities in \mathbb{Q}(N). They use the Casimir values C_F = \tfrac{N^2-1}{2N}, C_2(\mathrm{Sym}^2 V) = \tfrac{(N-1)(N+2)}{N} and C_2(\Lambda^2 V) = \tfrac{(N+1)(N-2)}{N}, together with the ribbon formula for the braiding on a summand of V \otimes V [kassel1995].

For item 4, the full twist acts on the irreducible summand indexed by \lambda as q^{2\,\mathrm{ct}(\lambda)}, where \mathrm{ct}(\lambda) is the sum of contents. The tensor product V \otimes \Lambda^N V is the summand \lambda = (2, 1^{N-1}), and \Lambda^N V is (1^N). So the monodromy of V around \Lambda^N V is q^{2\,\mathrm{ct}(2,1^{N-1}) - 2\,\mathrm{ct}(1^N)} = q^{2}. The braid has 2N crossings, so rescaling to c\,\sigma_i multiplies the monodromy by c^{2N}. The condition c^{2N} q^2 = 1 with c > 0 forces c = q^{-1/N}. \square

The value q^2 of the monodromy is computed on explicit Jimbo matrices for N = 2, 3 and from contents for all N.
rem:sl-n-color-frame-scope:
Remark Scope of the \mathrm{SU}(N) frame. Convention. A color observable is read with the framed generator \sigma_i^{\mathfrak{sl}} = q^{-1/N}\sigma_i of Proposition. Every other observable keeps the Hecke normalisation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The rescaling is not applied to the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) or to the writhe-normalised Markov trace. A uniform rescaling would multiply an unnormalised trace \mathrm{tr}_M(w) by q^{-\mathrm{wr}(w)/N}, where \mathrm{wr}(w) is the writhe of the word w, and would send z to q^{-1/N} z. Words of writhe zero are unaffected; words of nonzero writhe are not, so the scope matters.

The two-strand color factors. In the Hecke normalisation the two exchange channels of 3 \otimes 3 = \bar 3 \oplus 6 have log-exponents \pm 1. Their ratio is 1, against the group-theoretic |c_{\bar 3}/c_6| = 2. In the \mathrm{SU}(3) frame the log-exponents are -\tfrac43 and \tfrac23, so the ratio is 2 with both signs correct.

What the factor 2 was. The identity \log|\lambda_{\mathrm{S}}| + \log|\lambda_{\mathrm{A}}| = 0 for the Hecke eigenvalues, i.e. |\det \sigma_i| = 1 on V \otimes V, is the statement that the \mathfrak{u}_1 summand of \mathfrak{gl}_N = \mathfrak{sl}_N \oplus \mathfrak{u}_1 shifts both exponents by the same 1/N. It is a normalisation of the generator, not a structural obstruction to the color sector.

The nuclear channel is not repaired. The same frame at N = 2 gives the channel ratio (N+1)/(N-1) = 3. The nuclear T = 0 / T = 1 ratio it would have to reproduce is \approx 33.7. So the color frame does not supply the missing nuclear mechanism. This is a scope-limited negative: it says that this frame alone does not reach 33.7, not that framing cannot enter a nuclear closure.

Remark Prior art: q-integer differences are Alexander polynomials of (2n-1,2) torus knots. With symmetric q-integers [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}), Gavrilik observes that the differences [n]_q - [n-1]_q are the Alexander polynomials of the (2n-1,2) torus knots [gavrilik2001, \S 2, p. 2]:

[2]_q - 1 = \Delta_q\{3_1\},\qquad [3]_q - [2]_q = \Delta_q\{5_1\},\qquad [4]_q - [3]_q = \Delta_q\{7_1\}.

In the same section the torus knots 5_1, 7_1, 9_1, 11_1 are put in correspondence with the vector quarkonia s\bar s, c\bar c, b\bar b, t\bar t, as part of U_q(\mathfrak{su}_n) mass sum rules.

The identity is parameter-free and uses the same q-integers as the corpus. The assignment of the T(2,2k+1) family is a different matter: the flavour layer of the dictionary assigns it to leptons, and the trefoil–cinquefoil channel uses T(2,3) and T(2,5) for the colour tube, while Gavrilik assigns it to quarkonia. These are three different readings of one knot family. The paper takes q at a root of [n]_q - [n-1]_q, a root of unity such as e^{i\pi/5}, and compares the resulting mass relations with data at the per-cent level. It works on the unit circle, not at the real q_0, so it supplies the identity but no support for any one assignment.

The chapter cannot do without N = 3: the meson octet, the baryon multiplets, and every quark row of the dictionary are conditional on a three-dimensional partner, which is unavailable from a single fibre. As shown in the Standard Model appendix and in the flavour-charges remark, hypercharge is coupled to that same missing partner: on the split bundle F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q), tracelessness forces y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}y_2 with no free parameter, whereas without W_3^* the chapter reproduces I_3 alone and cannot close the Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation.

  1. The N = 3 problem. Schur--Weyl duality [jimbo1986] (Proposition) requires the fundamental representation to be 3-dimensional. The single-fibre tower has \dim V = 2 (the standard single-fibre construction; the Descartes condition \chi(\mathcal{A}) = -6 is compatible with but does not uniquely force N = 2). That N = 2 cannot host the decomposition is now proved (the alternating channel \binom{N}{3} vanishes iff N < 3, and the decuplet dimension forces N = 3) --- so the obstruction is settled and only the construction is missing. Owner ruling 2026-11-27: the flavour fundamental is now postulated as the axiom datum W of the flavoured definition, with condition (iii) kept for V; results that use W are consequences of the extended axioms, not derivations from the original ones. Open: construct a three-dimensional object W in the multi-fibre groupoid whose symmetric square \mathrm{Sym}^2(W) is irreducible (no singlet). The octonion G_2 route supplies a colour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} candidate that passes the gate: the singlet count 0 of \mathrm{Sym}^2(\mathbf{3}) is proved over \mathbb{Q}, together with \mathbf{3} \not\cong \bar{\mathbf{3}} (see the ledger). Whether it yields flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} is untested.

    What such a construction must supply is now a theorem, and it is one property rather than a list. Putting the two halves together: a three-dimensional object passing the gate must contain a complex-type irrep , and a category all of whose irreps are self-dual contains none — which is precisely the single-fibre case, since every \mathrm{SU}(2) irrep is self-dual. So the property a groupoid construction must exhibit is exactly the property one fibre lacks: non-self-duality. This yields a screening test : a candidate whose three-dimensional object is isomorphic to its own dual is dead, and can be discarded before its \mathrm{Sym}^2 decomposition is computed. It does not construct anything — Route A stays open — but it replaces "more structure" with a single checkable condition.

    The same condition is reachable from the row cap, independently. The Descartes characteristic \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 forces \mathrm{SU}(2), hence \dim V = 2, hence partitions of at most two rows, so the (1^3) block drops at n = 3 and a three-dimensional object cannot be a tensor power of the single fibre. That argument reaches non-self-duality without the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate and without the Frobenius--Schur trichotomy, as the gate-and-trichotomy argument reaches it without the Euler characteristic and without Schur--Weyl. A third route reaches the same negative from a different direction again: N \neq 3 follows from non-degeneracy of the fibre's volume form (\Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbf{1} forces N = 2), without the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate, the row cap or the Euler characteristic.

    The three are not three votes on one proposition, and the difference is what matters here. The row-cap and volume-form arguments bound the fibre: they say N = 2, so one fibre cannot supply a three-dimensional object. The gate-and-trichotomy argument bounds any candidate: it says which property a candidate must have, and so yields a test that can be applied to an object nobody has built yet. The negative is now over-determined; the screen is what is additive.

    That the search is confined to the groupoid level is now a theorem, not an extrapolation. The parity criterion decides the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate for a single irreducible summand, and a three-dimensional W need not be irreducible --- W = V_{1/2} \oplus V_0 has dimension 3, sits in the tensor category generated by the fibre, and is not an irrep, so that criterion does not reach it. The multiplicity form closes the case: counting singlets by Frobenius--Schur type, a passing W must be a sum of pairwise distinct even-dimensional irreps, hence \dim W is even. Since 3 is odd, no three-dimensional object of the single-fibre category passes the gate, reducible or not. Any N = 3 must therefore come from genuinely multi-fibre structure --- which is what the route above asserts, now with a proved invariant behind it (a scope-(b) exclusion, the invariant being the Frobenius--Schur indicator (-1)^{2j}). Even dimension is necessary, not sufficient: V_{1/2}^{\oplus 2} has dimension 4 and fails the gate too, so the parity invariant prunes candidates rather than characterising them. The octonionic candidate is no counterexample to this: it is not an object of the single-fibre category at all, arising instead from G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}), which is precisely why the parity exclusion leaves it standing.

    The mechanism behind that escape is now proved rather than asserted, and it is worth stating because it bounds how far the exclusion reaches. The parity argument runs through self-duality: every \mathrm{SU}(2) irrep satisfies V^* \cong V, so the cross terms V_i \otimes V_j contribute no singlet and the survivors are forced to be distinct even-dimensional irreps. A complex-type representation (\mathrm{FS} = 0, \mathbf{3} \not\cong \bar{\mathbf{3}}) pairs to a singlet only against its conjugate, so one whose conjugate is absent from the object passes the gate at any dimension, odd included --- and such an object is exhibited at dimension exactly 3. So the even-dimension exclusion above is a scope-(b) exclusion within the self-dual sector and is silent, not negative, outside it. This is the same non-self-duality that the colour construction already identifies as what the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate consumes.

    Nor is the fibre functor the missing knob. The single-fibre category admits fibre functors of every dimension n \ge 2 [bichon2003]: for E \in \mathrm{GL}_n with \mathrm{tr}(E^{-1}E^{t}) = -q - q^{-1} the comodule category of the bilinear-form quantum group B(E) is monoidally equivalent to that of \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SL}_2), and such E exist over \mathbb{R} at q_0 for every n \ge 3. So a three-dimensional image of V is available. It does not help, because a fibre functor is monoidal and therefore preserves the Clebsch--Gordan rule: under a three-dimensional fibre functor V^{\otimes 3} \cong V_{3/2} \oplus V_{1/2} \oplus V_{1/2} has dimensions 21 + 3 + 3, and under a fibre functor of any dimension the spin-0 summand the decomposition \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} requires is absent from V^{\otimes 3} by parity . Dimension is a property of the fibre functor; the multiplet structure is a property of the category. This closes the single-fibre reading of Route A --- the question does the category admit inequivalent fibre functors? is answered affirmatively and turns out not to bear on N = 3 --- and relocates the missing object to the category itself: an object W with \Lambda^3 W \neq 0, which the categorical volume constraint (Definition, condition 5) forbids for the fundamental.

  2. Hypercharge Y. The writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 is derived. The hypercharge Y is not: the writhe map is falsified as a Y assignment (proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ). Open: identify a second crossing invariant independent of the writhe. Battery (exploratory, not wired): of 10{,}000 helon-style assignments, 4 survive --- but that ratio carries no corroboration, and is not a 2500\!:\!1 filter. It is proved that the spectrum battery is exactly T = 3Q (the -2I_3 common to candidate and target cancels, leaving the defining equation of Q_{\mathrm{twist}}, not a test of it); the nucleon check is entailed by charge additivity and states one condition twice; and the \mathbb{Z}_6 condition never sees the assignment, so it filters nothing. Each flavour is thus filtered independently by one linear equation, and 4 = 1 \times 2 \times 2 \times 1 counts multisets with totals 3Q = (2,-1,0,-3) --- the "uniquely determined" u and electron multisets being the two totals that admit a single multiset. A parameter-free repair using the canonical ribbon twist (Q = c(\lambda)/3, c the content sum) was tested and fails: at n = 3 it gives the integer charges \{+1,0,-1\}, and no n \le 8 yields both quark charges ; scope-(a) for that reading only. The derivation gap is therefore the entire content: whether the twist multisets are forced by the categorical braid words (not just consistent with them) is the open content of the hypercharge conjecture, and nothing else in the battery constrains anything. In the split-bundle framing F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q) of the Standard Model appendix and the flavour-charges remark, tracelessness of \mathrm{diag}(y_2, y_2, y_3, y_3, y_3) forces y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}y_2, pinning the exterior-pair doublet hypercharge y_2 + y_3 = +\tfrac{1}{3} at y_2 = 1 with Killing Weinberg ratio 3/8, and separating \bar u (-\tfrac{2}{3}) from d (-\tfrac{1}{3}) despite their shared crossing sign -1. Hypercharge is thus reduced conditionally to the same missing object as item 1: constructing W_3 in the multi-fibre groupoid.

  3. Continuous G_2 completion. The discrete skeleton of \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} \subset G_2 = \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{O}) is verified (\mathrm{GL}(3, \mathbb{F}_2) \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,7) Fano symmetry of the associator), and so is the Lie-algebra level: \mathrm{Der}(\mathbb{O}) has dimension 14 and the stabilizer of e_1 has dimension 8, matching \dim S^6 = 14 - 8. The continuous Lie-group completion --- specifically the coset S^6 = G_2/\mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} --- not constructed here: the continuous Lie group G_2 is not available. This is an infrastructure obstruction, not a structural one.

  4. Flavour versus colour separation. The octonionic \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} is colour. The eightfold-way classification requires flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}. Whether these are the same, different, or related by a groupoid-level duality is open, and the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate cannot settle it.

    In particular the gate does not show that the two cannot both come from the same construction. That it excludes the icosahedral triple T_1 while the G_2 route passes compares two different objects and establishes only that those two differ, not that one construction cannot supply both roles. (The T_1 comparison is in the Schur--Weyl proposition, where it is now stated as a proved pass: the octonionic triple is complex type.)

    The failure is structural, not a repairable gap in the inference. It is proved that at dimension three, passing the gate is equivalent to carrying a complex-type irrep. Any two three-dimensional objects that both pass are therefore both complex type, and the gate has returned the same verdict for each --- two distinct such objects are exhibited. A flavour triple and a colour triple that each pass are, to this gate, indistinguishable.

    What the gate does establish is a class exclusion: no real or quaternionic construction reaches dimension three through it, so T_1's failure is a consequence of its Frobenius--Schur type and not a fact about the icosahedron. Whatever separates flavour from colour lies elsewhere --- as it does for the \mathbb{Z}/3 grading, which is likewise shown to be blind to the identification.

    The two blindnesses are one blindness. Both gates read only object-level data --- a dimension, a Frobenius--Schur type, a triality class --- and on that data the two triples coincide: the colour triple is the \mathbb{C}^3 of \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{O}) = \mathbb{R}\oplus\mathbb{C}^3, of complex dimension (7-1)/2 = 3; the flavour triple is the fundamental with Dynkin label (1,0), of Weyl dimension 2\cdot 1\cdot 3/2 = 3; both are complex type with triality 1. This is a class exclusion, and a proved one --- no gate reading only object data separates them, so there is no third such gate to look for. This is scope-(b), with the invariant named: equal data, equal verdict.

    Where a discriminator can live is item 7 below, not a further invariant of the object. The obstruction lifts as soon as a gate may also read which Young-symmetry channel of V^{\otimes 3} carries the physical state: colour occupies the totally antisymmetric channel \lambda = (1^3), flavour the symmetric \lambda = (3) for the decuplet and the mixed \lambda = (2,1) for the octet. These are distinct S_3-irreps, and a gate is exhibited that tells them apart. Item 7 already names this data, in the form "colour antisymmetric and spin symmetric force flavour symmetric"; items 4 and 7 are the same question seen from two sides.

    This locates the discriminator; it does not establish one. The channel assignment is an input, and item 7 records that the chapter derives neither the spin factor nor the colour antisymmetry that would supply it. What is settled is the negative half --- and the negative half is what redirects the search.

  5. Truncation mechanism. Why does the observable-scale symmetry reduce to a finite-dimensional Lie group rather than the full groupoid symmetry? Root-of-unity truncation is a candidate (T4), but no derivation of the specific root of unity from QOU axioms exists.

  6. Three generations. The A_2 root system and eightfold-way classification are generation-independent. Why there are exactly three generations of fermions is a separate open problem (T6), not addressed here.

  7. Spin--flavour--colour selection rule. The identification \lambda = (3) \leftrightarrow decuplet, \lambda = (2,1) \leftrightarrow octet (Proposition) currently matches dimensions and weights only. What physically forces the symmetric flavour channel for the spin-3/2 decuplet is antisymmetry of the total wavefunction once colour is included --- colour antisymmetric and spin symmetric force flavour symmetric. This chapter derives neither the spin factor nor the colour antisymmetry. Open: produce the spin degree of freedom and the colour-antisymmetry constraint from the braid structure, and show that together they determine the Young symmetriser. Compatibility with it is what the chapter currently establishes.

    The step between the inputs and the conclusion is now proved. If the three-quark wavefunction \chi(c)\,\varphi(r) is alternating under simultaneous permutation (Fermi statistics) and the colour factor \chi is a nonzero colour singlet, then \varphi is symmetric (symmetric_of_alternating_product); at N_c = 3 the colour-singlet channel is one-dimensional, spanned by the determinant (colourSinglet_eq_smul_det). What remains open is exactly the two inputs --- Fermi statistics and colour antisymmetry are not derived from the braid structure --- together with the cited Cauchy decomposition that pairs spin 3/2 with the decuplet (4 \cdot 10 + 2 \cdot 8 + 0 \cdot 1 = 56).

    This item is where item 4's discriminator lives. Item 4 asks what separates flavour from colour and shows that no invariant of the object can; the Young-symmetry channel named here is data about the role, and a gate is exhibited that reads it and does separate them. So deriving the colour-antisymmetry constraint would settle more than the selection rule --- it would supply the one input item 4 is missing.

  8. The Gell-Mann--Okubo deviation. The relation 4m_K^2 = 3m_\eta^2 + m_\pi^2 is not a target for derivation: it holds identically for any first-order octet breaking, whatever the mechanism, as proved in the meson mass-splitting remark. Reproducing it would therefore be no evidence for the framework. An unconstrained second-order polynomial in (I(I+1), Y) surjects onto every scalar residual and likewise carries no separating power. Replacing the classical Casimir by the parameter-free rational quantum Casimir d_q(I, Y) = [I]_q[I+1]_q - [Y/2]_q^2 [kleinkreisler1996] yields the (a,b,c)-free bar-even ratio (4M_K - 3M_\eta - M_\pi)/(M_\pi - M_\eta) = -((q - 1)/(q + 1))^2, equal to -2.7168 \times 10^{-3} at q_0. This predicts the observed signs on both the pseudoscalar meson octet (+) and the baryon octet (-) without free parameters, while accounting for only 1.21\% of the 6.43\% isospin-averaged meson deviation and 0.82\% of the -0.57\% baryon deviation. Open: the remaining \approx 6.3\% meson residual, dominated by \eta--\eta' singlet mixing and higher-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking. The former \approx 3.3\% comparison against \dim_q(\text{adjoint}) remains withdrawn as a category error (a dimension is not a mass splitting).

  9. Ocneanu/Markov trace parameter. The Markov trace \tau on H_n(q) involves a second parameter z (the trace parameter). sec:mass-endomorphism-opener-intro:

conj:mass-endomorphism:
Conjecture Mass endomorphism conjecture. The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) is defined categorically: it is the fibre functor image of the mass integrand (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho. The open problem consists of computing \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) explicitly—expressing its NF decomposition in the basis \{\mathbf{1}, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_-, e^-\} for specific braid words.

Scope: convenience target, not load-bearing

The scope of this conjecture is as follows:

  • Load-bearing series (independent of this conjecture): The categorical mass equals the infinite-series sum

      \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))\bigr|
  \;+\; \sum_{n \ge 0}\!\Bigl(
    \textstyle\sum_i \Phi_q(|\hat V_i^{(n)}|) + z^2 \sum_{(i,j)} \Phi_q(|\hat V_i^{(n)} \hat V_j^{(n)}|)
  \Bigr).

    This series decomposition combines the single-level Markov trace with the brane-tower quantum-dilogarithm sum and Frobenius co-Casimir pairing at z = q^3/(q^2+1). It does not depend on the closed-form conjecture below; every algebraic result that relies on the mass tower routes through this infinite series.

  • Convenience target (the conjectural content here): The conjecture posits the existence of a single finite-rank Hecke element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) whose Markov trace gives the full categorical mass. This element would collapse the infinite series into a closed-form evaluation. It serves symbolic computation but is not required for the structural derivations in this paper.

If this conjecture fails (no closed-form \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}} exists in finite-rank H_n(R, q)), the algebraic mass formula remains valid as the infinite series. Compute scripts attempting to materialise \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}} as a single element must truncate explicitly. Scripts that evaluate the infinite sum at q_0 (the dominant case) remain unaffected.

The scope of a failure is therefore exactly this: the tower formula remains correct as an infinite series, and the closed form is a convenience.

Statement

Conjecture (explicit mass endomorphism). The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) admits a closed-form NF decomposition in H_n(R, q) expressible in terms of the braid word \beta, the aether parameter q, and the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q. Specifically, the transient component satisfies:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\Phi^{\mathrm{trans}}(\beta)\bigr)
  =
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \Phi_q(z_i)
  =
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K_\beta)}{\hbar_q^2} -
  \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr)\bigr|,

where the spectral coordinates z_i of the blow-up centres are determined by the braid word and the Briggs--Klein chart.

Tower convergence

The electron mass \mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2})/\hbar_q^2 decomposes as a sum over brane levels n = 1, 2, \ldots, with level n contributing q^{-2n}/n^2 to \mathrm{Li}_2:

Levels Fraction of \mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2})
N = 1 73.9\%
N = 3 94.3\%
N = 10 99.75\%
N = 20 99.99\%

The tower converges in \sim 20 terms. This rate is consistent with t_P = 1/\hbar_q \approx 10 Reeb operations per Planck time. The first brane level alone provides 74\% of the electron mass; the remaining 26\% comes from higher jet prolongations.

Established results

Markov trace \neq Vol (the gap). The Jones--Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) is the Jones polynomial J(K; q)—a Laurent polynomial in q^{1/2}. The hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) is a transcendental number. They are different knot invariants: J(\text{trefoil}; q) = -q^{-4} + q^{-3} + q^{-1} while \mathrm{Vol}(\text{trefoil}) = 0.

The bridge between them is the Volume Conjecture [kashaev1997, murakami-murakami2001]:

  \lim_{N \to \infty}
  \frac{2\pi}{N}
  \log |J_N(K; e^{2\pi i/N})|
  =
  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K),

where J_N is the N-colored Jones polynomial. This limit involves evaluating at roots of unity (q = e^{2\pi i/N}, not generic q), the N-dimensional representation (not the fundamental), and an asymptotic limit (N \to \infty). Each step departs from the Hecke algebra at generic q.

The Habiro ring partially closes this gap. The colored Jones polynomials for all N coexist as a single element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. The algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) = \prod \hat{V}_i embeds into \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2}]}. Its evaluations at roots of unity collectively encode the hyperbolic volume via the Volume Conjecture. The mass at q_0 is a different specialisation of the same Habiro element. One evaluates directly at the aether parameter, rather than passing through roots of unity.

Encoding requirements for \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}

The brane tower \{A_n\} provides the categorical version of N \to \infty. Each brane level n contributes a transient trace \Phi_q(z_n), and the full mass sums over all levels. A mass endomorphism \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}} must encode this sum as a single element of H_n(R, q).

The quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(z) = \prod_{k=1}^{\infty}(1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1} is an infinite product. It is not a finite element of H_n(R, q) for any n. However, the brane tower truncates at finite N (determined by the knot crossing number), so the relevant sum is finite. The open question is whether this finite sum admits a closed-form expression in H_n(R, q).

Habiro-ring home for the tower limit. Even when the brane tower does not truncate finitely, the partial sums

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}^{(N)}(\beta)
  \;:=\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \Phi_q(z_i)

form a Cauchy sequence in the (q;q)_n-adic topology on \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. Each factor \Phi_q(z_i) has cyclotomic-denominator structure (the [k]_q in \Phi_q are cyclotomic), making successive partial sums agree modulo ((q;q)_n) for n growing with N. Therefore the limit

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}^{(\infty)}(\beta)
  \;\in\;\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}

exists as an element of the Habiro completion. It is well-defined purely algebraically, without analytic convergence. The non-archimedean realizations \{\rho_p\} recover the colored-Jones data via cyclotomic projection \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_N(q) without any complex-analytic limit.

The conjecture regarding a "closed-form expression in H_n(R, q)" asks a question in the finite-rank Hecke algebra. The N \to \infty tower limit asks a question in the Habiro completion \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}. Both are algebraic.

Two distinct convergence problems. The Habiro completion resolves the N \to \infty tower-limit problem in the ((q;q)_n)-adic topology on q. This is well-defined. At q_0 \approx 1.11 (real, |q| > 1, outside the natural boundary S^1), the Habiro evaluation agrees with the analytic infinite product.

A separate convergence problem affects the brane tower numerically. For the per-generator volumes |\hat{V}_i| of low isotopes, all values sit at |\hat{V}_i| \in [0.85, 1.0]—at the boundary of the z-radius of convergence of \Phi_q(z) = \prod (1 - q^{-k} z)^{-1}. Numerically \Phi_q(0.989) \approx 6.7 \times 10^5 and \Phi_q(1) \approx 9 \times 10^5. The Habiro framework addresses completion in q, not in z. It does not regularize the |\hat{V}|\approx 1 behaviour.

Two partial mitigations are documented, though neither universally closes the gap:

  1. Magic-shell structural term. Add a separate \Delta_{\text{shell}}(Z, N) contribution to the binding formula distinguishing closed-shell stabilization from the brane-tower transient.

  2. Markov-trace audit on {}^3\mathrm{He}. Verify |\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}})| at q_0 against the canonical reducer to confirm the structural gap is real and not a Markov-trace mis-count.

The brane tower contribution remains not computable in closed form for |\hat{V}|\approx 1 under the original conjecture. The descended Markov trace plus Frobenius co-Casimir alone empirically reproduces the binding within \sim 30\% for low isotopes.

The quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q = \sum \log \lvert\hat{V}_i\rvert is the candidate for binding-energy differences between nuclei (Q-values at Level 0); it does not give single-nucleon absolute masses, and the binding magnitude remains open.

prop:pairing-gauge-fluctuation-massless:
Proposition Pure-gauge fluctuations of a pairing are zero modes of the contraction action. Let \mathbf{C} be a monoidal category that is preadditive and R-linear over a commutative ring R, and let A^\vee, A be objects with an exact pairing A^\vee \dashv A (so that A is a right dual of A^\vee in the sense of a rigid monoidal category), with coevaluation \eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A^\vee \otimes A. The field space of Frobenius pairings is the R-module \mathcal{P} = \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^\vee \otimes A, \mathbf{1}). For a co-pairing \eta and a linear functional \varepsilon \colon \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \to R, the contraction action is the quadratic form

  S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(T) \;=\; \varepsilon(T \circ \eta)^2 ,
  \qquad
  \frac{\delta S_{\eta,\varepsilon}}{\delta T}(\delta) \;=\; 2\,\varepsilon(T\circ \eta)\,\varepsilon(\delta\circ\eta),

on \mathcal{P}, where the variational derivative is twice the symmetric bilinear form of S_{\eta,\varepsilon}; it satisfies the exact Taylor identity S(T+\delta) = S(T) + \frac{\delta S}{\delta T}(\delta) + S(\delta).

For f \in \mathrm{End}(A^\vee) with right adjoint mate f^{\vee} \in \mathrm{End}(A), the pure-gauge fluctuation of a background pairing \lambda \in \mathcal{P} is

  \delta_f \lambda \;=\; \lambda \circ \bigl( f \otimes \mathrm{id}_A \;-\; \mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes f^{\vee} \bigr).

For every f, every background \lambda and every field T \in \mathcal{P}:

  S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(\delta_f\lambda) = 0,
  \qquad
  \frac{\delta S_{\eta,\varepsilon}}{\delta T}(\delta_f\lambda) = 0,
  \qquad
  S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(T + \delta_f\lambda) = S_{\eta,\varepsilon}(T).

More generally, for any quadratic action S on an R-module, invariance under translation by a direction g holds if and only if S(g) = 0 and g lies in the radical of \delta S/\delta T for every T; such directions form a submodule. No hypothesis on 2 \in R is used.

The argument is one line: (f \otimes \mathrm{id}_A) \circ \eta = (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes f^{\vee}) \circ \eta is a standard property of the mate, so \delta_f\lambda \circ \eta = 0, and the contraction action sees \delta_f \lambda only through \delta_f\lambda \circ \eta.

The handedness of the Frobenius pairing. The exact pairing above has evaluation A \otimes A^\vee \to \mathbf{1}, which is not the Frobenius pairing A^\vee \otimes A \to \mathbf{1}. A non-degenerate Frobenius pairing instead makes A \dashv A^\vee exact, with the Frobenius pairing as evaluation and a coevaluation \tilde\eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A^\vee. If \mathbf{C} is a braided monoidal category, with braiding \beta, then \beta_{A,A^\vee} \circ \tilde\eta \colon \mathbf{1} \to A^\vee \otimes A is a co-pairing, and the same three conclusions hold for it, with the gauge fluctuation now \lambda \circ ( f \otimes \mathrm{id}_A - \mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes {}^{\vee}\! f), where {}^{\vee}\! f \in \mathrm{End}(A) is the left adjoint mate of f for A \dashv A^\vee. The argument is the same, with the mate identity transported through the naturality of \beta.

Scope. The contraction action has rank at most one, so its radical contains far more than the pure-gauge directions; the proposition says that gauge directions are among the zero modes, not that they exhaust them. Without a braiding, a non-degenerate Frobenius pairing supplies no co-pairing \mathbf{1} \to A^\vee \otimes A, and that case is not covered.

If the Frobenius pairing is read as a metric, a fluctuation \delta\lambda of the pairing is the categorical analogue of a metric perturbation h_{\mu\nu}. Under that reading, the proposition is the algebraic shadow of the familiar statement of linearised gravity that pure-gauge perturbations h \mapsto h + \mathcal{L}_\xi \bar g cost no action: the infinitesimal automorphism f plays the role of the vector field \xi, the combination f \otimes \mathrm{id} - \mathrm{id} \otimes f^{\vee} that of the Lie derivative of the background, and the vanishing of S(\delta_f\lambda) together with the radical condition is what "no mass term along gauge directions" means for a quadratic action.

What is not shown, and would be needed before the reading could be called a derivation:

  2. that the physical (non-gauge) fluctuations transform as a spin-2 isotypic piece, i.e. the symmetric traceless part of \mathrm{Sym}^2 of a spin-1 object;

def:mass-identity:
Definition Mass (Frobenius form of the mass integrand). Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (quantum observable universe) and let \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} be its recursive brane tower (recursive brane tower). Let \mu, \eta be the multiplication and unit of the Frobenius--Hopf object A, let \Delta \colon A \to A \otimes A be the comultiplication and let \int_A \colon A \to \mathbf{1} be the Frobenius form. The mass integrand is the endomorphism

  \Psi = (\textstyle\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \colon A \to A .

The inertial mass of a morphism \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A (a "closed cycle" in the Frobenius--Hopf object) is the norm of the composite \mathbf{1} \xrightarrow{\varrho} A \xrightarrow{\Psi} A \xrightarrow{\int_A} \mathbf{1}:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
    \textstyle\int_A \circ\, \Psi \circ \varrho
  \bigr\rVert,

where \lVert \cdot \rVert is the norm on R induced by the Frobenius pairing (Frobenius pairing). The mass measures the resistance of the Frobenius--Hopf structure to transporting the cycle \varrho through the comultiplication.

The composite is an element of \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) = R, so no trace is applied. Two facts fix its value. First, \Psi is left multiplication by the fixed element u = \Psi \circ \eta, so \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert \int_A (u \cdot \varrho) \rVert. Second, when the Frobenius form is the counit \varepsilon, as it is for the coalgebra a Frobenius form induces, u = \eta and \Psi = \mathrm{id}_A, so \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \lVert \int_A \varrho \rVert.

The categorical trace of the endomorphism L_\varrho \circ \Psi, where L_\varrho is left multiplication by \varrho, is a different quantity. It equals \int_A (u \cdot \varrho \cdot c), with c = \mu \circ \mathrm{coev} the Casimir element of the self-duality of A. Under a fibre functor to free R-modules this is the regular trace of A, which is not a Markov trace.

Non-abelian holonomy and Temperley–Lieb state sum. For a word w = [g_1, \dots, g_k] of segment transports g_i \colon \mathbf{1} \to A, the cycle is the non-abelian multiplicative integral \varrho = \mathrm{hol}(w) = g_1 * \cdots * g_k in the convolution monoid (\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, A), *, \eta), satisfying \mathrm{hol}(w_1 \mathbin{+\!+} w_2) = \mathrm{hol}(w_1) * \mathrm{hol}(w_2). Multiplication takes place in \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, A) before applying the linear functional \int_A \circ \Psi (giving \int_A (u \cdot \mathrm{hol}(w))) or the categorical trace \mathrm{tr}(L_{\mathrm{hol}(w)} \circ \Psi) = \int_A (u \cdot \mathrm{hol}(w) \cdot c). When A acts on V^{\otimes n} (V = R^2) via Jimbo's R-matrix \check R, each signed crossing transport T(\sigma_a^{\pm 1}) decomposes over R into the identity channel and the Temperley–Lieb cup-cap generator e_a = q \cdot 1 - \check R_a (e_a^2 = (q + q^{-1}) e_a): T(\sigma_a) = q \cdot 1 - e_a and T(\sigma_a^{-1}) = q^{-1} \cdot 1 - e_a. Expanding the ordered holonomy product \mathrm{Hol}(\ell_1 \cdots \ell_k) = T(\ell_1) \cdots T(\ell_k) over binary states s \in \{0, 1\}^k expresses the Markov trace on B_n as the state sum

  \textstyle\int_A \rho(\beta_\ell)
  = \sum_{s \in \{0, 1\}^k} w_{\mathrm{TL}}(\ell, s) \, \textstyle\int_A \mathrm{TL}(\ell, s),

where w_{\mathrm{TL}}(\ell, s) = \bigl(\prod_{j : s_j = 0} c(\ell_j)\bigr) (-1)^{|s|} (c(\sigma_a) = q, c(\sigma_a^{-1}) = q^{-1}) and \mathrm{TL}(\ell, s) = \prod_{j : s_j = 1}^{\longrightarrow} e_{a_j}. The all-zero state s \equiv 0 contributes the per-crossing scalar product \prod_{j=1}^k c(\ell_j), while the states s \neq 0 collect the Temperley–Lieb loop contractions.

Braid classes. When the cycle is the image \varrho = \rho(\beta) of a braid \beta on n strands and \int_A is the Jones–Markov trace, the mass is read on braid classes: braids on any number of strands modulo conjugation and positive or negative stabilisation. The trace is cyclic and is multiplied by fixed units under the two stabilisations, so its framing-corrected form

  (1 + q^2)^{n} \, q^{-n - 2 w(\beta)} \textstyle\int_A \rho(\beta),

with w(\beta) the writhe of \beta, is constant on each class. This form, not the raw trace, defines the mass of a braid class. That braid classes correspond to isotopy classes of oriented links is the theorem of Alexander and Markov [alexander1923, markov1936], which names the classes and enters no statement here.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows spans the algebraic→archimedean wall. The pre-archimedean Frobenius mass is valued in the generic ground ring R (the Frobenius norm \lVert x\rVert_F = \langle x, x\rangle_F stays in R). The post-\tau scalar mass is the archimedean realisation R \to \mathbb{R}, x \mapsto \lVert x\rVert, obtained by evaluating the Frobenius norm at the aether parameter q = q_0. The R \to \mathbb{R} realisation map inherently crosses the wall and cannot be made \mathbb{R}-free or generic-only. It is acknowledged here rather than splitting it off.
